entities.summary:
The 2011 Russian legislative election was a nationwide vote held on December 4, 2011, which saw the re-election of Vladimir Putin as the Prime Minister of Russia. The election was significant in the arc of world history as it marked a turning point in the country's democratic transition. The election was also notable for the widespread allegations of electoral fraud and the subsequent protests that unfolded in Moscow's Bolotnaya Square, marking a major escalation of the country's post-Soviet democratic movement. The election saw the United Russia party, led by Putin, secure a majority in the State Duma, consolidating their power and setting the stage for further authoritarian reforms in the country.

The election was marred by allegations of vote rigging and electoral manipulation, with opposition parties and independent observers accusing the ruling party of using their control of the electoral commission to disenfranchise opposition voters. The election also saw the rise of protests in Moscow and other major cities, with thousands of opposition supporters taking to the streets to demand a recount and an end to Putin's rule. The protests were eventually put down by the authorities, but they marked a significant escalation of the country's democratic movement and set the stage for further protests and unrest in the years that followed.

The legacy of the 2011 Russian legislative election can be seen in the country's continued slide into authoritarianism, with Putin's party consolidating their power and opposition voices being silenced. The election also marked a major shift in the country's relationship with the West, with the US and EU responding to the allegations of electoral fraud with sanctions and diplomatic pressure. In the end, the election marked a major turning point in the country's post-Soviet democratic transition, setting the stage for further protests, unrest, and authoritarianism in the years that followed.
